title: Building a Cultural Perspective on Doctor-Patient Conversations

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing interactional cultural markers (e.g., directiveness, verbosity, participation structure, response styles) across real, simulated, and synthetic LLM-generated doctor-patient conversations from Indian and US clinical contexts.

Comparing the cultural fidelity and interactional deviations of synthetic clinical conversations generated in a medium-resource language (Hindi) versus a low-resource language (Telugu) against their respective real or simulated baselines.
Analyzing synthetic deviations in interactional markers (such as patient reassurance-seeking, certainty, and doctor empathy) across generated male- and female-patient consultation scenarios.
